messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-us-east-1 saturated (90% queue growth). Autoscaler failed to add nodes: quota_limit_hit. Affected service: inference-serving-prod. Trigger: sustained queue length > 250 for 3m. Paging @infra_oncall and @sre_lead :rotating_light:

infra_oncall: I'm on it, grabbing logs. initial observation: queue depth spiked ~15:02 UTC, correlates with canary rollout of model v33.

sre_lead: tagging @ml_serving and @eng_runtime — is v33 expected to increase KV cache usage / context growth?

ml_serving: yes, v33 introduced per-request extended context+kv prefetching for system prompts. We saw local perf but not this magnitude. Rolling rate was small though.

eng_runtime: looking at autoscaler events: "scale_up_attempt" -> "rejected: quota.exhausted" from cloud provider at 15:05:12. Also several nodes failed warmup and were evicted due to oom during prefill.

product_ops: heads up, CS reports 3 customers seeing 503s and degraded latency on hosted API.

customer_success: confirmed — two customers (ACME, BrightShop) reported spikes starting ~15:03 UTC, some requests time out after 30s. We're drafting a message.

sre_lead: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle v33 traffic to 25% 2) route heavy-context customers to dedicated pools 3) rollback canary if throttle doesn't reduce queue in 5m.

ml_serving: implementing throttle rule now: set model.route.weight(v33)=0.25 via routing service. Pushing config:
```
PUT /routing/prod/models/v33
{ "weight": 0.25, "reason": "emergency throttle due to kv amplification" }
```
Applying — 15:07:02.

eng_runtime: also adding a short-lived fallback to v32 for contexts > 8k tokens. Command: `trafficctl route --model v32 --conditions "context_tokens>8000" --duration 30m`

infra_oncall: cloud quota team called — we hit GPU quota per-region. Request to increase pending but ETA 2-3h. No immediate extra capacity.

sre_lead: ok, need other mitigations. eng_runtime can we disable prefetch/warmup for v33 to reduce warmup OOM?

eng_runtime: yes, toggling prefetch off for v33: `model-config set v33 prefetch=false` — done at 15:08:40. Expect fewer OOMs on node start.

deploy-bot: deploy v33 canary update completed (prefetch disabled) — build #2024.15 at 15:08:41.

ml_serving: monitoring metrics: queue depth decreased from 320 -> 180 within 2m after throttle and fallback rules. Latency p50 improved but p95 still high for some routed requests.

sre_lead: good. customer impact: ACME reported 45 failed requests in 5m window; BrightShop ~120. We should prepare incident notification.

product_ops: drafting external incident note: "Temporary throttling of v33 after increased GPU utilization during rollout; some customers experienced timeouts. Engineers implementing rollback and mitigations."

customer_success: I'm sending targeted DMs to ACME and BrightShop with interim mitigation steps and ETA.

infra_oncall: new action: purge in-memory KV warmups for idle models to free GPU memory on nodes: `kvcachectl purge --age>10m --region us-east-1` executed 15:12:05. Reports show ~12% GPU memory reclaimed across pool.

eng_runtime: added short-term autoscaler override to allow burst nodes from backup quota set (if provider allows) — it will retry once per minute for 10m. If still rejected, fallback to routing policies. Enabled at 15:12:45.

ml_serving: queue depth now 90 and stabilizing. Rolling back heavy canary traffic to v32 gradually. No further OOMs observed in new starts.

sre_lead: summary for oncall handoff: primary mitigations taken: throttled v33 to 25%, routed large-context >8k to v32, disabled prefetch, purged idle kv warmups, enabled autoscaler retry. Current status: stable but degraded for some customers. ETA to full recovery depends on canary rollback or staggered redeploy.

infra_oncall: leaving primary oncall — handing to @sre_lead for the next 2 hours.

sre_lead: taking handoff. Next steps: 1) continue monitoring queue and p95 latency 2) prepare permanent fix (v33 config change to reduce kv fanout or roll v33 back entirely) 3) open postmortem and customer impact assessment.

product_ops: can we estimate number of affected API calls and minutes of degraded service? ml_serving: can you surface counts?

ml_serving: quick numbers 15:02-15:15 UTC: ~2.1M tokens impacted, ~9k API calls throttled/errored. I'll add a more formal breakdown to the postmortem ticket.

customer_success: customers acknowledged temporary mitigation. No SEV-level escalations open at this time.

sre_lead: thanks everyone. I'll convert this thread into an incident ticket and link pager logs. Please add any notes re: config tests for v33 changes.

eng_runtime: note for postmortem: in future, gate prefetch by canary % and run load tests that exercise kv prefetch paths with pooled GPUs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=stabilized, severity=major, assigned=sre_lead, incident_id=INC-2025178901, start=5178901234, last_update=5178901880

sre_lead: closing slack thread for active mitigation; will continue async updates on INC-2025178901.
